cross_item_pattern.rule: In a "between which two consecutive levels did the change increase the LEAST/MOST" or "which consecutive pair does NOT satisfy a minimum change" item, pick the option naming the pair at the top end of the tested range (the highest pair of values listed). Applied without the passage: the option set lists the pairs, so the reader just takes the highest pair.
cross_item_pattern.evidence: Picks the key on 3 of 3 such items across 3 passages (P1, P2, P9), against 1/4 by chance each (expected 0.75; P(3/3)=1.6%). Every consecutive-step table in the batch is either concave with saturation (P1 times, P2 levels) or convex accelerating (P9 power loss), so the extreme step always sits at the top pair whichever direction the stem asks. The rule is backed by a diminishing-returns/accelerating-cost prior a test-wise student would also hold. No counter-example in the batch: there is no consecutive-pair item whose key is not the top pair. Related but not counted: P9-Q5 (ratio greatest at the first, lowest step) and P4-Q5 (knee at 30 cm) follow the same concave shapes.
